/*
 * FrostCore — Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JS engine boundary
 * Public C API (Stage 1: Lifecycle + Eval)
 *
 * GlacioJS includes only this header; never includes quickjs.h directly.
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_H
#define FROSTCORE_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Allocator vtable
 *
 * Pass a filled frost_alloc to frost_runtime_create(). Every allocation
 * made by the runtime (including the GC heap) routes through these
 * pointers. userdata is forwarded opaquely on every call — use it for
 * per-isolate arenas, tracing hooks, capacity accounting, etc.
 *
 * calloc is optional: if NULL, the runtime falls back to alloc+memset.
 * malloc_usable_size is optional: if NULL, exact sizes are used instead
 * of the OS slab size, which is slightly less efficient.
 *
 * If alloc is NULL altogether, frost_runtime_create() uses the default
 * system allocator (equivalent to passing malloc/free/realloc).
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr); /* no userdata — POSIX convention */
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Runtime handle — opaque
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Lifecycle
 *
 * frost_runtime_create — alloc may be NULL to use the system allocator.
 *   Returns NULL on allocation failure.
 *
 * frost_runtime_destroy — frees everything owned by this runtime.
 *   Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.
 *
 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Minimal eval surface (integration handshake for GlacioJS)
 *
 * Evaluates `source` as a JS global script expression.
 * Returns  0 on success.
 * Returns -1 on error; *out_error receives a malloc'd (system malloc)
 *   NUL-terminated UTF-8 message — caller must free() it.
 *   out_error may be NULL if the caller doesn't want the message.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_H */

description: FrostCore project purpose, architecture, and relationship to GlacioJS

---

FrostCore is a custom JS engine layer built on top of quickjs-ng. It is NOT a rewrite — it establishes an extraction boundary over the living quickjs-ng C codebase.

**Why:** GlacioJS (Layer 2 scheduler/isolate manager) needs a pluggable allocator, explicit multi-runtime lifecycle, and no hidden globals — none of which quickjs-ng's public API exposes cleanly enough. FrostCore adds that thin boundary.

**Architecture:**
- `frost/` — FrostCore overlay (never touches upstream quickjs-ng files)
- `frost/include/frostcore.h` — the ONLY header GlacioJS may include
- `frost/src/frostcore.c` — adapter/wrapper implementation
- `frost/tests/` — isolation smoke tests
- `frost/CMakeLists.txt` — builds `frostcore.lib` + `quickjs_static.lib`
- `build.sh` / `build.ps1` — end-to-end build + test scripts

**How to apply:** All GlacioJS integration goes through `frostcore.h`; never let GlacioJS import `quickjs.h` directly.

Planned stages: Stage 1 (done) → Stage 2: GlacioJS isolate scheduler → Stage 3: stdlib separation → Stage 4: bytecode modularity.

# FrostCore

**Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JavaScript engine boundary layer.**

FrostCore wraps [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) with a thin C API that gives the embedding layer — GlacioJS — explicit control over memory allocation, runtime lifecycle, and JS evaluation. It is not a rewrite of the engine; it is an extraction boundary on top of a living upstream codebase.

---

## What FrostCore Is

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Per-runtime pluggable allocator | Stage 1 |
| Explicit `create` / `destroy` lifecycle (no hidden globals) | Stage 1 |
| Multiple runtimes coexisting in one process | Stage 1 |
| Minimal `eval` surface for integration testing | Stage 1 |
| GC algorithm changes | Not in scope |
| Parser/bytecode modularization | Stage 3+ |
| Stdlib separation | Stage 3+ |
| C++ wrapper | Not in scope |
| Task/isolate scheduler | GlacioJS Layer 2 |

---

## Repository Layout

```
FrostCore/
  quickjs.c / quickjs.h    — upstream quickjs-ng engine (do not edit)
  libregexp.c / libunicode.c / dtoa.c — upstream support files
  CMakeLists.txt / meson.build        — upstream build (untouched)
  README.txt                          — original quickjs-ng README

  frost/                   — FrostCore overlay (all Stage 1 work lives here)
    include/frostcore.h    — public C API — the ONLY header GlacioJS imports
    src/frostcore.c        — implementation
    tests/smoke_test.c     — isolation + leak smoke test
    Makefile               — builds libfrostcore.a without CMake

  build.sh                 — Unix: build + run smoke test
  build.ps1                — Windows: build + run smoke test
```

---

## Public API (Stage 1)

```c
#include "frostcore.h"

/* Allocator vtable — all fields except alloc/free/realloc are optional */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr);
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* Pass NULL to use the system allocator */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
   *out_error is malloc'd — caller must free() it. */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);
```

---

## Building

### Unix (clang required)

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh          # Release
./build.sh Debug
```

Produces `frost/build/libfrostcore.a` and runs the smoke test.

### Windows (PowerShell, clang in PATH)

```powershell
.\build.ps1
.\build.ps1 -BuildType Debug
```

Produces `frost\build\frostcore.lib` and runs the smoke test.

### Manual (from `frost/`)

```sh
make              # builds libfrostcore.a + smoke test, runs test
make lib          # libfrostcore.a only
make clean
```

---

## Upstream

FrostCore is built on [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) (MIT).

# FrostCore Stage 1 — Build System
# Produces: build/libfrostcore.a  build/frost_smoke[.exe]
#
# Usage:
#   make              — build lib + smoke test, run test
#   make lib          — libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         — build everything, run smoke test
#   make clean        — remove build/
#
# Variables (override on command line):
#   CC      — C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      — archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   — output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     — optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

# Source root is the parent of this Makefile (the repo root)
ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage1\"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c

FROST_SRCS := src/frostcore.c

SMOKE_SRCS := tests/smoke_test.c

# Object files land in build/
QJS_OBJS   := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))

LIB        := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke

# Detect Windows (MSYS/Git Bash / native) and add .exe suffix
ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    # msvcrt doesn't have -lm but it doesn't need it either
    LDLIBS    :=
else
    LDLIBS    := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)

# Smoke test binary
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# FrostCore static library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure build dir exists before any .o is built
$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (include path: repo root)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# frostcore wrapper object
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# smoke test object
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

/*
 * FrostCore — Stage 2: Subsystem Registration API
 *
 * After frost_runtime_create_bare(), GlacioJS selects which JS built-ins
 * to install by calling zero or more frost_register_std_*() functions.
 * Each group is idempotent: calling it twice on the same runtime is safe
 * (returns 0 on the second call, nothing re-installed).
 *
 * Dependency rules (enforced at registration time):
 *   std_collections  requires  std_core
 *   std_async        requires  std_core
 *   std_time         requires  std_core
 *   std_io           requires  std_core   (uses Object, String internally)
 *
 * If a dependency is missing, the register call returns -1 with a
 * descriptive message in *out_error.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   frost_runtime *rt = frost_runtime_create_bare(&alloc);
 *   frost_register_std_core(rt, NULL);
 *   frost_register_std_async(rt, NULL);
 *   // console is intentionally absent — not available in this isolate
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H
#define FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H

#include "frostcore.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Registration return convention (same as frost_eval):
 *   0   success (or already registered — idempotent)
 *  -1   failure; *out_error is malloc'd UTF-8 message, caller must free()
 *       out_error may be NULL.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_core
 *
 * Installs: Object, Function, Array, String, Number, Boolean, Symbol,
 *           Error hierarchy, Iterator, Math, eval(), RegExp, JSON, Proxy,
 *           Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet.
 *
 * This is the minimal set for sensible JS execution. Every other
 * subsystem depends on it.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_core(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_collections
 *
 * Installs: TypedArrays (Int8Array … Float64Array, DataView, ArrayBuffer,
 *           SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics), WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_collections(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_async
 *
 * Installs: Promise, async/await support, queueMicrotask,
 *           ArrayBuffer.transfer, atob/btoa, DOMException.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_async(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_time
 *
 * Installs: Date, performance (performance.now / timeOrigin).
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_time(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_io
 *
 * Installs: console.log, print() (global).
 * Output goes to stdout. This is the only subsystem that touches I/O.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 *
 * Note: This does NOT install the full quickjs-libc module system
 * (no setTimeout, no fs, no os). Those are GlacioJS Layer 3 concerns.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_io(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_all
 *
 * Convenience: installs all subsystems above in dependency order.
 * Equivalent to frost_runtime_create() but on a bare runtime.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_all(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Introspection
 *
 * frost_subsystems_registered — bitmask of what has been registered.
 * Useful for assertions and debug logging in GlacioJS.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define FROST_STD_CORE        (1u << 0)
#define FROST_STD_COLLECTIONS (1u << 1)
#define FROST_STD_ASYNC       (1u << 2)
#define FROST_STD_TIME        (1u << 3)
#define FROST_STD_IO          (1u << 4)

unsigned int frost_subsystems_registered(const frost_runtime *rt);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H */

### API summary

```c
frost_runtime *rt = frost_runtime_create_bare(&alloc);  // zero stdlib

frost_register_std_core(rt, NULL);        // Object, Array, Math, JSON, RegExp, Map…
frost_register_std_collections(rt, NULL); // TypedArrays, WeakRef

// — or —

frost_subsystems_registered(rt);          // → FROST_STD_CORE | FROST_STD_ASYNC | …
```

### Non-obvious fix documented

`frost_runtime_create_bare()` must call `JS_AddIntrinsicEval()` even though it installs nothing visible in JS. Without it, `ctx->eval_internal` stays NULL and every `frost_eval()` call — even `"1+2"` — throws `"eval is not supported"` at the C level. `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` sets the function pointer; `JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects` (inside `frost_register_std_core`) is what puts `eval` into the JS global scope.
